removes nothing, so it reached the pull request describing what the

fix(review): Keep each block of changed lines apart

Two additions with an unchanged line between them are two blocks, not
one. Read as a single list they were adjacent, so a suggestion spanning
the gap was taken for code the patch had already applied and dropped.

Both sides of the comparison are now normalized the same way, so a blank
line in a suggestion no longer stops it lining up with the patch.

comment.body:
If `line.value` retains its trailing newline character (e.g. `\n` or `\r\n`), joining the raw values with `\n` will introduce extra empty lines when split and normalized in `_normalize_snippet`. Stripping trailing line breaks beforehand ensures that the run is normalized correctly without empty-line artifacts.

```suggestion
        runs: List[List[str]] = []
        current: List[str] = []
        for line in hunk:
            if line.is_added if added else line.is_removed:
                current.append(line.value.rstrip("\r\n"))
            elif current:
                runs.append(current)
                current = []
        if current:
            runs.append(current)
        return [cls._normalize_snippet("\n".join(run)) for run in runs]
```

commits.message:
feat(review): Speed up and trace premium reviews

Premium reviews now share parsed diffs, indexes and source reads within one
review instead of repeating them, and start static analysis and overviews
alongside discovery, so large pull requests spend less time waiting.

Model calls report admission wait, duration, tokens and errors, and an
optional trace collaborator receives context and finding events, so a slow
or failing review can be explained after the fact. Search and skill
selection can be routed to their own model profiles.

A structured response cut off by its output budget is retried once at twice
the budget, control characters in model JSON no longer fail parsing, and
multi-line findings keep their end line.

feat(review): Add evaluation policies and doubt handling

Evaluators can judge findings under a behavioral or a premises policy, both
off by default. Under premises, a claim that the change breaks an explicit
requirement is established by quoting the requirement and the violating
code, while a claim about runtime consequences has its trigger, reach,
impact and certainty verified, and the finding is ranked by the softest
reading its supporters verified. A doubt that only concerns the suggested
fix no longer keeps an established defect from being supported.

Discovery can optionally hand concerns it nearly dropped to evaluation
instead of discarding them. Evaluation reads candidates in batches grouped
by file, and duplicate reports of one defect in different files merge only
when the supporting evaluations agree.

feat(review): Add investigation discovery for large changes

Discovery can split a change into investigations that each fit one model
call, instead of reading the whole change several times. A change gets at
least as many investigations as independent readings and more when its
parts would not fit the reading budget, up to a configurable limit; a
change needing more is refused before any model is asked, with the reason.
A single file larger than the budget is investigated alone rather than
dropped.

feat(review): Add repository context, change digest and callers

Reviews can now be given more of the repository than the changed lines,
each part behind its own setting and off by default: the repository's
documentation, found by format and ranked by nearness to the change; the
manifests and source the changed files import; and the functions that call
each changed definition and those it calls. Callers and callees come from
the code index where it resolved them and are otherwise matched by name in
the source for every language the parser reads, and each says how it was
found.

Investigations can also receive a digest of the whole change, listing every
changed file with the definitions its changed lines fall in, so a change in
one investigation's files is visible to the others.

Hosted reviews list the repository's files once per review so documentation
can be discovered, and the large-change investigation path is exercised
through the snapshot API. Copied third-party test sources now carry their
licences.

feat(index): Derive calls from SCIP indexes

A SCIP index records which symbols each definition references but not
which it calls. A reference to a function or method from inside another
function's enclosing range is now recorded as that function calling it,
and definitions keep their name, file and lines, so callers of changed code
can come from an index a repository supplies, compiler accurate for the
languages its indexers cover. An index filed at the revision under review
is preferred to one filed for the repository as last read.

feat(review): Raise the default reading budget to 50,000 tokens

Each model call now reads up to 50,000 tokens of a change instead of
15,000, so a large change is read in about a third as many calls, each
repeating the instructions and context less often. The window the models
accept is far larger than either figure. Repositories can still set their
own budget.

refactor(review): Name settings for what they do

A setting that is only on or off is now a toggle named for what turning it
on does: split large changes, group related files, read direct dependencies
first, include the change digest and evaluate uncertain findings. The
evaluation policy keeps its choice of values, renamed to say what each does.
None of these settings had shipped, so no stored value changes meaning.
